learning_outcomes.text: Design systems and carry out projects on manufacturing systems based on the described processes and verify (measure) their dimensional and surface quality.
Acquire knowledge in manufacturing systems and materials, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing versatility to adapt to new situations.
Express and communicate ideas and systems related to manufacturing systems and materials.
Understand and prepare professional technical documentation, in the context of activities related to manufacturing systems and materials.
Master the basic manufacturing processes used in Engineering.
Master the basic concepts of materials and their relationship with related aspects of Engineering.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to production and manufacturing systems: history of manufacturing processes. Development of manufacturing systems. Manufacturing industries and products. Classification of manufacturing processes. Forming operations, property improvement operations, surface processing operations, assembly operations.

Metrology: definition and importance of metrology. Units and measurement standards. International System of Units. Johansson gauges. Surface plates and verification rules. Angle measurement. Trigonometric metrology. Comparison measurement.

Casting processes: general fundamentals. Disposable mold and permanent mold casting processes. Sand molding. Mold and core manufacturing. Calculation of distribution systems. Defects in cast parts. Inspection.

Material removal processes: factors influencing material removal. Cutting speed, feed, depth of cut, cutting force, cutting power. Taylor, Kronenberg and Denis relations. Machining time. The lathe, description and applications. The milling machine, description and applications. The grinder, description and applications.

Welding processes: fundamentals, classification and applications of welding processes. Solid-state welding. Fusion welding: Arc welding, resistance welding, oxy-fuel gas welding, other fusion welding processes. Brazing and soldering. Control and testing of welds.

assessment_methods.method: Completion of practices and submission of relevant reports
Preparation and presentation of a work related to manufacturing systems and materials, including monitoring of work progress
Written exam: a component on the theory of the subject and another on problems and practical cases

assessment_rules: To average the three sections, a minimum of 4 out of 10 points must be achieved on the exam. If the Exam Grade is 4 points or higher, the final grade will be the weighted arithmetic mean of the three sections. If the Exam Grade is less than 4 points and the weighted arithmetic mean is 5.0 points or higher, the final grade will be 4.9 points. If the Exam Grade is less than 4 points and the weighted arithmetic mean is less than 5.0 points, the final grade will be that weighted arithmetic mean. If the student does not attend the Exam, the grade will be 'Not presented'.
